scope: Synthetic saved audio through T24E390, local ASR, real signed-in backend, production conversation controller and overlay. Typed probes explicitly exclude audio/ASR. No human-interview certification.
reviewScope: Unblinded manual review of all twenty actual brief/detailed causal followups, each with identical explicit frozen context. Exact text replay with a signed-in backend; neither native ASR nor independent expert certification. Objectives run sequentially; provider drift remains possible.

renderer.scope: Actual served renderer shared by native variant comparisons; native core binaries remain separate.

capabilities.validatedBy: Startup completes a real stream using these settings. Codex additionally checks supportedReasoningEfforts.

outputDevice: 1 - T24E390 (2- AMD High Definition Audio Device)

measurements.scope: Observed fixture workload; sample p95 is not a population guarantee. Missing/incorrect/incomplete rows remain in counts and have no successful latency. HTTP actual wire write remains unknown when not instrumented.
measurements.nonFaultNonObserverScope: Excludes requested transport-fault probes and disclosed observer interference. All rows remain in correctness/completion/missing counts and overall latency distributions. This exclusion alone does not certify a healthy warm path.
measurements.nonFaultProbeScope: Excludes requested transport-fault probes, including unsupported or unconfirmed injections. Does not independently certify every remaining sample as a healthy warm connection.

allFollowupUsefulP95Ms.scope: Missing, incorrect and unverified useful delivery rank after finite correct delivery; missing latency is never replaced with a timeout value.

panelTransitions.scope: Sampled viewport transitions and native/host clock bounds. Upper bounds allow prior text until the first observed clearing/new-generation paint; an unobserved blank paint may make the actual interval shorter. Lower bounds use only observed old-generation paint after acceptance. Not a universal stale-output certificate.

rows.name: brief-why-1
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: CUDA groups 32 threads into a warp so the GPU can issue one instruction to many threads at once. If threads take different branches, each path executes with only its participating threads active, reducing parallel efficiency.

review.note: One instruction across many threads explains grouping, masked branches reduce efficiency.
review.usefulPrefix: CUDA groups 32 threads into a warp so the GPU can issue one instruction to many threads at once.

rows.name: brief-why-2
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a warp’s 32 threads share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the warp, with a mask selecting which lanes execute it. When threads take different branches, each path runs with only its participating lanes active, reducing parallel efficiency.

review.note: Shared instruction issue and masks explain the actual divergence claim.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a warp’s 32 threads share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the warp, with a mask selecting which lanes execute it.

rows.name: brief-why-3
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a warp shares an instruction stream across 32 threads. When threads take different branches, the GPU executes each required path with nonparticipating lanes masked off. That’s branch divergence, and it reduces parallel efficiency.

review.note: Shared instruction stream and masked nonparticipating lanes explain throughput loss.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a warp shares an instruction stream across 32 threads.

rows.name: brief-why-4
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because threads in a warp share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the warp, with an active mask controlling which lanes execute it. When threads take different branches, each path runs with only its relevant lanes active, reducing parallel efficiency.

review.note: Shared instruction issue and active mask give the causal mechanism.
review.usefulPrefix: Because threads in a warp share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the warp, with an active mask controlling which lanes execute it.

rows.name: brief-why-5
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a warp shares an instruction stream: the GPU issues an instruction to its active thread lanes together. When threads take different branches, it masks off the lanes that don’t belong to each path, executes the required paths, then reconverges—so divergence can reduce throughput.

review.note: Shared stream/masked paths explain divergence; reconvergence does not claim implicit lockstep synchronization.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a warp shares an instruction stream: the GPU issues an instruction to its active thread lanes together.

rows.name: brief-why-6
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because threads in a warp share instruction-issue hardware. When they take different branches, the GPU executes each path with only its participating threads active, reducing parallel efficiency. The 32-thread size is NVIDIA’s architectural choice.

review.note: Shared instruction hardware explains masked paths;32 is architectural choice.
review.usefulPrefix: Because threads in a warp share instruction-issue hardware.

rows.name: brief-why-7
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: A warp groups 32 threads so the GPU can issue one instruction to all of them together, reducing control overhead. When threads take different branches, each path runs with only its participating threads active, so divergence reduces efficiency.

review.note: One instruction/group reduces control overhead; masked branches reduce useful participation.
review.usefulPrefix: A warp groups 32 threads so the GPU can issue one instruction to all of them together, reducing control overhead.

rows.name: brief-why-8
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a warp’s 32 threads share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the warp, with an active mask selecting which lanes execute it. When threads take different branches, the GPU executes the different paths with different masks, so divergent paths reduce parallel efficiency.

review.note: Shared issue with different masks explains reduced parallel efficiency.
review.usefulPrefix: Because a warp’s 32 threads share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the warp, with an active mask selecting which lanes execute it.

rows.name: brief-why-9
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because the 32 threads in a warp share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the active lanes together. When threads take different branches, it executes each needed path with the other lanes masked off, which can reduce efficiency.

review.note: Shared issue for active lanes explains separate needed paths and lost efficiency.
review.usefulPrefix: Because the 32 threads in a warp share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the active lanes together.

rows.name: brief-why-10
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because the 32 threads in a warp share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the warp’s active lanes. When threads take different branches, it executes each needed path with nonparticipating lanes masked off, reducing parallel efficiency.

review.note: Shared issue and inactive lanes give a substantive causal explanation.
review.usefulPrefix: Because the 32 threads in a warp share instruction issue: the GPU issues an instruction to the warp’s active lanes.
